item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Monday 13 July 2026 — FSB touts foiled airbase drone plot as Moscow hit by mass strike
item.description:
ZBloggers Monitor

Monday 13 July 2026 — daily read on 10 pro-Kremlin military Telegram channels

Pro-Kremlin channels blanketed the day with a coordinated FSB claim of having thwarted Ukrainian FPV-drone attacks on strategic airbases, while simultaneously acknowledging a 300+ drone Ukrainian assault on the Moscow region that killed three civilians. Sentiment split sharply: triumphant on internal security (net +75) but grim on Ukrainian strikes (net -67).

🚩 Russia-internal sentiment jumps +135 to net +75. The swing is driven almost entirely by the multi-channel FSB airbase-plot claim (16 internal posts, 13 positive), amplified by Putin's People's Front forum appearance. The uniformity suggests centrally coordinated messaging rather than organic mood.

🚩 Mobilisation rumours and Putin criticism stay silent. No posts touched mobilisation rumours or criticism of Putin; the only 'mobilisation' subtopic post praised the Popular Front as a supply mechanism, and Putin coverage was entirely favorable.

  1. FSB claims it foiled FPV-drone plot against airbases (✓ multiple channels)
    At least seven channels ran near-identical claims that the FSB pre-empted Ukrainian FPV-drone attacks on strategic airbases in Amur and Chelyabinsk regions, seizing 24 drones with 'Western'/'NATO' neural-network components and detaining operatives. The heavy uniformity and Rybar's 184k-view lead post suggest a centrally distributed security-services narrative rather than independent reporting. source ↗
  2. Mass Ukrainian drone strike on Moscow region kills three (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels reported Ukraine launched 300+ (one post cited 350+) drones at the Moscow region; Russia claimed 81-89 intercepted. Kotsnews and WarGonzo said three civilians were killed and six wounded, with fires in five houses in Pionersky — figures MoD-adjacent and unconfirmed. This was the day's most-viewed post (Two Majors, 288k). source ↗
  3. Russian strikes on Chornomorsk/Odesa ports; internal skepticism (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels claimed Russian drones and precision weapons damaged Chornomorsk grain/oil terminals, ferries and cargo ships over two days, allegedly halting Kernel exports. Notably, Rybar's own analyst (188k views) questioned the strike claims, citing lack of visible damage — a rare intra-channel dissent worth flagging. source ↗
  4. Britain sanctions GRU officers and Rybar staff (◌ single source)
    Rybar reported UK sanctions targeting Russian GRU officers and its own channel staff over cyber operations. The founder responded that sanctions rest on 'distorted information' and that three team members had already left before the designation — a self-referential deflection. source ↗
  5. European-Ukrainian air defense coalition framed as NATO cover (✓ multiple channels)
    Several channels flagged formation of a nine-nation-plus-Ukraine anti-ballistic-missile coalition and a 'NATO-Ukraine integrated air defense' effort, framing Western tech as operating 'under civilian cover.' Two Majors also cited Germany funding 50,000 AI-enabled Shrike FPV drones for Ukraine. source ↗

Mood of coverage: 51% positive / 9% neutral / 40% negative across 67 substantive posts.

    Multiple channels claimed Russian Geran-4 drones and missiles hit port infrastructure and military cargo at Odesa and Chornomorsk, with Poddubny and WarGonzo claiming three vessels destroyed. Rybar cited an implausible figure of '404 S-400 cruise missiles'; all figures are channel-sourced and unconfirmed. source ↗

Tone was split: upbeat on Russian strikes and frontline gains, defensive and irritated on tankers and refinery damage.

🚩 Russia internal cools 39 points. Despite an upbeat FSB counter-terror narrative around the Rostov airfield plot, net sentiment fell to +38 as introspective essays on wartime honesty and lists of 'absurd' administrative fines added neutral-to-negative tone.

    Two Majors ran multiple posts describing a persisting Azov Sea campaign against Russian tankers, claiming a fifth consecutive day of attacks and citing a fuel-logistics problem; one post claimed Russia intercepted 376 drones while Ukraine allegedly hit 14 tankers. WarGonzo said a Turkish tanker was struck. All figures are channel/MoD-sourced and unverified. source ↗
